## Provisioning Profiles

### `appitool apple profiles list`

Lists provisioning profiles on Apple Developer Portal (name, Portal ID, UUID, type, state, expiration date).

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `-n, --name <name>` | Filter by provisioning profile name. |
| `-l, --limit <count>` | Maximum number of items to return. |

### `appitool apple profiles create`

Creates and optionally downloads a provisioning profile on Apple Developer Portal.

| Option | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-b, --bundle-id <id>` | **Required** | Application Bundle Identifier. |
| `-n, --name <name>` | `match <type> <bundle-id>` | Provisioning profile name. |
| `-t, --type <type>` | `appstore` | Profile type: `appstore`, `development`, `adhoc`, `enterprise`, `developer_id`. |
| `-p, --platform <platform>` | `ios` | Target platform: `ios`, `macos`, `tvos`, `catalyst`. |
| `--certificate-id <id>` | First active matching cert | Certificate Portal ID to embed in the profile. |
| `--device-ids <ids>` | All enabled matching devices | Comma-separated device Portal IDs for `development`/`adhoc` profiles. |
| `-o, --output <path>` | — | File path to save the generated `.mobileprovision` / `.provisionprofile`. |

```bash
appitool apple profiles create -b com.example.app -t adhoc -o ./AdHoc_com.example.app.mobileprovision
```

### `appitool apple profiles delete`

Deletes a single provisioning profile by name, UUID, or Portal ID.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `-n, --name <name>` | Provisioning profile name. |
| `--uuid <uuid>` | Provisioning profile UUID. |
| `--portal-id <id>` | Provisioning profile Portal ID. |

### `appitool apple profiles prune`

Deletes all `INVALID` (and optionally expired) provisioning profiles from Apple Developer Portal.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Preview candidate profiles without deleting them. |
| `--include-expired` | `false` | Also prune expired profiles in addition to `INVALID` profiles. |

```bash
appitool apple profiles prune --include-expired --dry-run
```

## Signing Certificates

### `appitool apple certificates list`

Lists certificates registered on Apple Developer Portal with status (`ACTIVE` / `EXPIRED`), type, serial number, and expiration date.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `-t, --type <filter>` | Filter by certificate type (`distribution`, `development`, `developer-id`, `ios-distribution`, `ios-development`, `mac-distribution`, `mac-development`). |
| `-l, --limit <count>` | Maximum number of items to return. |

### `appitool apple certificates create`

Generates an RSA 2048-bit private key and CSR locally, submits it to Apple Developer Portal, and saves the `.cer` and private `.key` (plus optional `.p12` and Keychain import).

> [!WARNING]
> Keep the generated private key safe—Apple does not store private keys and they cannot be re-downloaded.

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-t, --type <type>` | `distribution` | Certificate type: `development`, `distribution`, `developer-id`, `ios-development`, `ios-distribution`, `mac-development`, `mac-distribution`, `mac-installer`. |
| `-n, --name <cn>` | Auto-generated | Common Name (CN) for the CSR subject. |
| `-o, --output <dir>` | `~/.appitool/certs/{type}/` | Output directory for `.cer`, `.key`, and `.p12`. |
| `--p12` | `false` | Export a `.p12` (PKCS#12) archive containing certificate and private key. |
| `--p12-password <pass>` | `appitool` | Password for the exported `.p12` archive. |
| `--save-to-keychain` | `false` | Import certificate and private key into the `appitool` Keychain and delete `.p12` once verified. |

```bash
appitool apple certificates create -t distribution --p12 --save-to-keychain
```

### `appitool apple certificates delete`

Revokes/deletes a certificate from Apple Developer Portal by Portal ID, name, or serial number.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--portal-id <id>` | Certificate Portal ID. |
| `-n, --name <name>` | Certificate name. |
| `--serial-number <serial>` | Certificate serial number. |

### `appitool apple certificates prune`

Deletes/revokes all expired certificates from Apple Developer Portal.

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Preview expired certificates without revoking them. |
| `-t, --type <type>` | — | Filter pruning by certificate type (e.g. `distribution`, `development`). |

## Users & Invitations

> [!NOTE]
> Managing App Store Connect team users and invitations requires an API key with the **Admin** role. The `ACCOUNT_HOLDER` role cannot be assigned or modified via the API.
>
> **Supported Role Keys (comma-separated):** `admin`, `app-manager`, `developer`, `finance`, `sales`, `marketing`, `customer-support` (alias: `support`), `access-to-reports` (alias: `reports`), `create-apps`, `cloud-managed-developer-id`, `cloud-managed-app-distribution`, `generate-individual-keys`.

### `appitool apple users list`

Lists active team users in App Store Connect.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--username <email>` | Filter by username (Apple ID email). |
| `-r, --roles <roles>` | Filter by comma-separated roles (e.g. `admin,developer`). |
| `-l, --limit <count>` | Maximum number of items to return (omit to fetch all). |

```bash
appitool apple users list
appitool apple users list -r admin,developer
```

### `appitool apple users invite`

Sends an email invitation to add a new user to your App Store Connect team.

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-e, --email <email>` | **Required** | Invitee email address. |
| `--first-name <name>` | **Required** | Invitee first name. |
| `--last-name <name>` | **Required** | Invitee last name. |
| `-r, --roles <roles>` | **Required** | Comma-separated roles to assign (e.g. `developer,app-manager`). |
| `--visible-apps <apps>` | — | Comma-separated App Store Connect App IDs or bundle IDs to grant access. |
| `--all-apps-visible` / `--no-all-apps-visible` | `true` (or `false` if `--visible-apps` is set) | Grant visibility to all apps. |
| `--provisioning-allowed` / `--no-provisioning-allowed` | Role default | Allow access to certificates, identifiers, and profiles. |

```bash
appitool apple users invite \
  -e dev@example.com \
  --first-name Jane \
  --last-name Doe \
  -r developer \
  --visible-apps com.example.app \
  --provisioning-allowed
```

### `appitool apple users update`

Updates an active team user's roles, app visibility, or provisioning access (identify user with `--id` or `--username`).

| Option / Flag | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--id <id>` | User resource ID in App Store Connect. |
| `--username <email>` | User username (Apple ID email). |
| `-r, --roles <roles>` | Comma-separated roles to assign. |
| `--visible-apps <apps>` | Comma-separated App Store Connect App IDs or bundle IDs for visible apps. |
| `--all-apps-visible` / `--no-all-apps-visible` | Grant or restrict visibility to all apps. |
| `--provisioning-allowed` / `--no-provisioning-allowed` | Allow or disallow access to certificates, identifiers, and profiles. |

```bash
appitool apple users update --username dev@example.com -r app-manager --all-apps-visible
```

### `appitool apple users delete`

Removes an active team user from App Store Connect (identify user with `--id` or `--username`).

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--id <id>` | User resource ID to remove. |
| `--username <email>` | User username (Apple ID email) to remove. |

```bash
appitool apple users delete --username dev@example.com
```

### `appitool apple invitations list`

Lists pending team user invitations in App Store Connect.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `-e, --email <email>` | Filter by invitee email address. |
| `-r, --roles <roles>` | Filter by comma-separated roles. |
| `-l, --limit <count>` | Maximum number of items to return (omit to fetch all). |

```bash
appitool apple invitations list
```

### `appitool apple invitations cancel`

Cancels a pending user invitation in App Store Connect (identify invitation with `--id` or `-e, --email`).

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--id <id>` | Invitation resource ID to cancel. |
| `-e, --email <email>` | Invitee email address whose pending invitation should be canceled. |

```bash
appitool apple invitations cancel -e dev@example.com
```

## Assets (`appitool apple assets`)

Manages the App Store product page images of a version, per localization:

| Kind | `-t, --type` values | API |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Screenshots | screenshot device slots (`iphone-67`, `ipad-pro-129`, `iphone-duo`, … — see `assets types`) | `APP_SCREENSHOT` / `IMESSAGE_APP_SCREENSHOT` placements with the slot's placement group (e.g. `IPHONE_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_LARGE_PROFILE`) |
| Product page header (iOS 27+) | `header` | `PRODUCT_PAGE_HEADER_ASSET` placement |
| Search results (iOS 27+) | `search` | `APP_STORE_SEARCH_RESULTS_ASSET` placement |

All types use the App Store Connect **Asset Library** (API 4.6.1): an image is uploaded into the app's Asset Library (reserve → chunked upload → commit, then processing) and then *placed* on a version localization. Removing a placement keeps the image in the Asset Library. Screenshot slots hold up to 10 images in display order (reordered with placement ordering requests); `header` / `search` hold exactly one image, and placing a new one replaces the current one. Screenshots need an editable version; header/search can also be changed on a live version. Videos are not supported yet.

Everything lives in one local tree: `~/.appitool/assets/<project>/apple/<locale>/<type>/`, where `<type>` is a screenshot slot key (up to 10 images) or `header` / `search` (exactly one image). When [`STORE_ASSETS_PATH`](https://appitool.appibara.com/guide/configuration#store-assets-apple-assets-google-assets) is set, the tree is `<STORE_ASSETS_PATH>/apple/<locale>/<type>/` instead (default paths below then refer to that folder).

All `assets` subcommands (except `types` and `specs`) accept shared app-resolution options:

| Option | Default / `.env` Fallback | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-b, --bundle-id <id>` | `APPLE_BUNDLE_ID` or auto-detected from Xcode project | Target application bundle identifier |
| `--app-id <id>` | — | Numeric App Store Connect App ID (takes precedence over `--bundle-id`) |
| `-p, --platform <platform>` | `ios` | Target platform (`ios`, `macos`, `tvos`, `visionos`) |
| `--app-version <ver>` | Auto-selects editable version (or latest for `list`) | Explicit App Store version string (e.g. `1.2.0`) |

### `appitool apple assets list`

Lists screenshots per device slot (in display order) and header / search results placements on the resolved App Store version, with placement IDs, dimensions, and states. Screenshots in device slots appitool does not know yet are reported with their placement group.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--locale <locale>` | Filter by App Store locale (e.g. `en-US`, `tr`). Omit to list all localizations. |
| `-t, --type <type>` | Filter by screenshot slot (e.g. `iphone-67`, `ipad-pro-129`, `iphone-duo`), `header`, or `search`. |
| `--asset-library` | Instead of the regular view, list every Asset Library placement on each localization (all placement types, including screenshot placements, with their placement group). |

```bash
appitool apple assets list -b com.example.app
appitool apple assets list -b com.example.app --app-version 1.2.0 --locale en-US -t iphone-67
```

### `appitool apple assets upload`

Uploads screenshots (to an editable App Store version, e.g. `PREPARE_FOR_SUBMISSION`; new screenshots are added at the end of their slot, and slots that would exceed 10 images are rejected before any change) and header / search results images either from explicit flat image paths (`--locale` and `-t` required) or symmetrically from a `<locale>/<type>/` directory tree defaulting to `~/.appitool/assets/<project>/apple/` (`--locale` and `-t` optional filters). Each `header` / `search` folder must contain exactly one image; it replaces that localization's current placement (a new placement is created first and the old one removed; if App Store Connect rejects a second placement, the old one is removed first). A file used for several localizations is uploaded to the Asset Library once.

| Option / Flag / Argument | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--locale <locale>` | — | App Store localization locale (e.g. `en-US`, `tr`). Required for flat files; optional filter for `<locale>/<type>/` trees. |
| `-t, --type <type>` | — | Screenshot slot (e.g. `iphone-67`, `ipad-pro-129`, `APP_IPHONE_67`, `iphone-duo`), `header`, or `search`. Required for flat files; optional filter for directory trees. |
| `--replace` | `false` | Remove the existing screenshots of each target slot before uploading. For `<locale>/<type>/` trees, also writes each folder's sync manifest. Header/search slots are always replaced. |
| `--sync` | `false` | Mirror `<locale>/<type>/` folders using `.appitool-manifest.json` (see [Asset sync](#asset-sync)). Cannot be combined with `--replace`; requires a directory tree, not explicit files or a flat folder. |
| `--all-locales` | `false` | Place one explicit `header` or `search` file on every localization of the version (requires a file and `-t header` / `-t search`; cannot be combined with `--locale` or `--sync`). |
| `--wait-processing` / `--no-wait-processing` | `true` (`--wait-processing`) | Wait for App Store Connect to process each uploaded image. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate files and preview upload targets without contacting App Store Connect. With `--sync`, reads App Store Connect (no changes) and prints the sync plan. |
| `<paths...>` | `~/.appitool/assets/<project>/apple/` | Optional PNG/JPEG file(s), flat directory, or `<locale>/<type>/` directory tree. |

```bash
# Bulk-upload all locales and types from ~/.appitool/assets/<bundle-id>/apple/
appitool apple assets upload --replace

# Bulk-upload only en-US slots from the default per-project directory
appitool apple assets upload --locale en-US --replace

# Upload flat directory images for a single locale and display type
appitool apple assets upload \
  -b com.example.app \
  --locale en-US \
  -t iphone-67 \
  --replace \
  ./screenshots/ios/en-US/iphone-67/

# Preview, then apply, only the local changes since the last download/sync
appitool apple assets upload --sync --dry-run
appitool apple assets upload --sync

# Use one header image for every localization
appitool apple assets upload --all-locales -t header ./header.png

# Set the en-US search results image
appitool apple assets upload --locale en-US -t search ./search.png
```

#### Asset sync

`download`, `upload --replace` (directory trees), and `upload --sync` write a `.appitool-manifest.json` into each `<locale>/<type>/` folder. For screenshot folders it records the slot identity (`<version-id>/<locale>/<placement-group>`) and, for every file, the matching placement ID and the SHA-256 of the local file. For `header` / `search` folders it records the placed Asset Library image ID and the file's SHA-256.

`header` / `search` folders under `--sync`: unchanged file whose image is still placed → nothing is sent; changed file (or a different image placed) → upload and place; no manifest and nothing placed → upload and place; no manifest but an image is placed → error (run `download` first, or upload without `--sync` to replace it). Header/search slots are planned before any screenshot change.

Screenshot folders:

`upload --sync` plans every slot before changing anything; any planning error aborts the run without remote changes. Per slot:

| Local state | Action |
|:---|:---|
| File in manifest, checksum unchanged | Keep (no upload). |
| File in manifest, checksum changed | Replace: upload and place the new file, then remove the old placement (removes first when the slot already has 10 screenshots). |
| File renamed but content unchanged | Keep (matched by checksum). |
| File not in manifest | Add. |
| Manifest entry whose file was removed | Remove the placement from App Store Connect. |
| Screenshot on App Store Connect not in the manifest | Left untouched (warning) and placed after the managed screenshots. |

After uploads, the slot order is set to the local file-name order (`01_…`, `02_…`) with a placement ordering request, and the manifest is rewritten.

| Manifest | Remote slot | Result |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Missing | Empty | Bootstrap: upload all files in file-name order, write the manifest. |
| Missing | Has screenshots | Error: run `download` first or use `--replace`. |
| For a different slot or version | — | Error: run `download` again or delete the manifest and use `--replace`. |

Slots that would exceed App Store Connect's limit of 10 screenshots → error before any change. A `<locale>/<type>/` folder with no images is skipped, so emptying a folder does not clear its slot; use `apple assets delete` for that.

### `appitool apple assets download`

Downloads screenshots from App Store Connect (`imageAsset.templateUrl` at full resolution) into `<output>/<locale>/<type>/01_<name>.<ext>`, and placed header / search results images into `<output>/<locale>/<header|search>/<name>.<ext>`. By default, files are stored per project under `~/.appitool/assets/<bundle-or-app-id>/apple/`. Existing leading order prefixes (`01_...`) are stripped before applying the current store order prefix so round-tripping download → upload → download does not double-prefix filenames.

Downloaded files are the images served by Apple's CDN, which can be smaller than the originally uploaded files (same dimensions, different encoding). Each slot folder also gets a `.appitool-manifest.json` for [`upload --sync`](#asset-sync). Screenshots in device slots appitool does not know yet are skipped with a warning. Images written by a previous download whose screenshots no longer exist on App Store Connect are removed; other local images are kept and reported (`upload --sync` would add them).

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--locale <locale>` | — | Filter by App Store locale (e.g. `en-US`, `tr`). Omit to download all locales. |
| `-t, --type <type>` | — | Filter by screenshot slot (e.g. `iphone-67`, `ipad-pro-129`, `iphone-duo`), `header`, or `search`. |
| `-o, --output <dir>` | `~/.appitool/assets/<project>/apple/` | Custom destination root directory. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Preview target local paths and CDN URLs without downloading files. |

```bash
# Download all locales and display types for the project to ~/.appitool/assets/<bundle-id>/apple/
appitool apple assets download

# Download only en-US iPhone 6.7" screenshots into a custom folder
appitool apple assets download -b com.example.app --locale en-US -t iphone-67 -o ./downloads/ios
```

### `appitool apple assets delete`

Removes one placement by ID, or all assets for `--locale` (and optional `--type`). Removing a placement takes the image off the localization; the image stays in the Asset Library. Screenshots require an editable version; with `-t header` / `-t search` a live version can be used. Guarded in CI mode.

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--id <placement-id>` | — | Placement ID to remove, as shown by `assets list` (mutually exclusive with `--all`). |
| `--locale <locale>` | — | App Store localization locale when deleting with `--all`. |
| `-t, --type <type>` | — | Optional filter when deleting with `--all`: a screenshot slot (e.g. `iphone-67`, `iphone-duo`), `header`, or `search`. Omit to remove all types (screenshots, header, and search). |
| `--all` | `false` | Remove all assets matching `--locale` (and optional `--type`). |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Preview matching assets without removing them. |

```bash
appitool apple assets delete --id "<placement-id>"
appitool apple assets delete -b com.example.app --locale en-US -t iphone-67 --all --dry-run
```

### `appitool apple assets types`

Lists all supported screenshot slots (the 33 App Store Connect screenshot display types plus `iphone-duo` and `imessage-iphone-duo`) with their CLI aliases and Asset Library placement groups, plus `header` and `search` (no credentials required).

```bash
appitool apple assets types
```

### `appitool apple assets specs`

Shows Apple's current image specs live from `appAssetLibraryRefData` (needs only Apple credentials):

- **header / search:** size or size range, aspect ratio, formats, maximum file size, alpha, universal assets.
- **screenshot:** one entry per device slot with its `-t` key, display class (e.g. `IPHONE_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_LARGE_DISPLAY`), platform, screen dimensions, placement group, maximum count per version, and the accepted sizes and formats.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `-t, --type <kind>` | `screenshot`, `header`, `search`, or one screenshot slot (e.g. `iphone-67`, `iphone-duo`). Omit to show all. |

```bash
appitool apple assets specs
appitool apple assets specs -t header
```

---

## Metadata (`appitool apple metadata`)

Manages App Store listing text as one plain-text file per field: `<root>/<locale>/metadata/<field>.txt`, where `<root>` is `$STORE_ASSETS_PATH/apple/` or `~/.appitool/assets/<project>/apple/` (the same folder as `apple assets`; image commands ignore `metadata/` folders). There is one current set of files per locale (no per-version folders); git history keeps earlier texts.

| File | Field | Limit | Lives on |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `name.txt` | Name | 30 | App info localization |
| `subtitle.txt` | Subtitle | 30 | App info localization |
| `privacy_policy_url.txt` | Privacy Policy URL | — | App info localization |
| `privacy_choices_url.txt` | Privacy Choices URL | — | App info localization |
| `description.txt` | Description | 4000 | Version localization |
| `keywords.txt` | Keywords (comma-separated) | 100 | Version localization |
| `promotional_text.txt` | Promotional Text | 170 | Version localization |
| `whats_new.txt` | What's New | 4000 | Version localization |
| `marketing_url.txt` | Marketing URL | — | Version localization |
| `support_url.txt` | Support URL | — | Version localization |

**App-level fields** (one value for all languages) live in `<root>/metadata/<field>.txt`:

| File | Field | Lives on | Editable when |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `copyright.txt` | Copyright | Version | Version editable |
| `primary_category.txt`, `primary_subcategory_one.txt`, `primary_subcategory_two.txt`, `secondary_category.txt`, `secondary_subcategory_one.txt`, `secondary_subcategory_two.txt` | Categories (App Store category IDs such as `PRODUCTIVITY`, `GAMES_ACTION`; validated against `appCategories` for the platform) | App info | App info editable |
| `review_contact_first_name.txt`, `review_contact_last_name.txt`, `review_contact_phone.txt`, `review_contact_email.txt` | App Review contact | Version (App Review details) | Version editable |
| `review_notes.txt` | App Review notes (max 4000) | Version (App Review details) | Version editable |
| `review_demo_account_required.txt` | `true` / `false` | Version (App Review details) | Version editable |
| `review_demo_account_name.txt` | Demo account user name | Version (App Review details) | Version editable |
| `content_rights_declaration.txt` | `DOES_NOT_USE_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT` or `USES_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT` | App | Any time |
| `accessibility_url.txt` | Accessibility URL | App | Any time |

The demo account password is a secret: it is never written to or read from files. Set `APPLE_REVIEW_DEMO_PASSWORD` (e.g. in `.env`) to upload it; it is sent only when it differs from the current value and is masked in all output. App Review details are created when the version has none yet.

**Which version and app info:** the version is resolved like `assets` (editable version preferred, `--app-version` to pick one, otherwise the latest). The app info is the editable one while a new version is being prepared, otherwise the live one. Every command prints the version and app info state it reads from or writes to. Name, subtitle, and privacy changes need an editable app info and go live with the next version; version fields need an editable version, except `promotional_text`, which can also change on a live version.

All subcommands accept the shared app options (`-b, --bundle-id`, `--app-id`, `-p, --platform`, `--app-version`).

### `appitool apple metadata list`

Shows the app-level fields (`[app]`, password masked) and every field per localization with its character count and limit (long texts are shortened).

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--locale <locale>` | Show only this locale (app-level fields are skipped). |

### `appitool apple metadata download`

Writes each non-empty field to `<locale>/metadata/<field>.txt` and app-level fields to `metadata/<field>.txt` (with a trailing newline; the demo account password is never written). Existing files are overwritten.

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--locale <locale>` | — | Download only this locale (app-level fields are skipped). |
| `-o, --output <dir>` | `$STORE_ASSETS_PATH/apple/` or `~/.appitool/assets/<project>/apple/` | Metadata root directory. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Preview files without writing them. |

### `appitool apple metadata upload`

Reads `<locale>/metadata/*.txt` and `metadata/*.txt`, compares each file with the store value (surrounding whitespace ignored, `\r\n` treated as `\n`), and sends only fields that differ. Missing and empty files are ignored, so a blank file never clears a store field. Everything is planned first: length limits, value checks (categories, content rights, `true`/`false`), and editability are checked before any change, and any error aborts the run. Local locales that are not localizations of the app/version are skipped with a warning (add the language in App Store Connect first).

| Option / Flag / Argument | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--locale <locale>` | — | Upload only this locale (app-level fields are skipped). |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Print the per-field changes without sending them. |
| `<path>` | `$STORE_ASSETS_PATH/apple/` or `~/.appitool/assets/<project>/apple/` | Metadata root containing `<locale>/metadata/` folders. |

```bash
appitool apple metadata download
# edit ~/.appitool/assets/<bundle-id>/apple/en-US/metadata/whats_new.txt
appitool apple metadata upload --dry-run
appitool apple metadata upload
```

<!-- source: commands/google.md -->

# `appitool google`

Direct management of Google Play Console store visuals and resources via the Google Play Developer API v3.

All `google assets` subcommands (except `types`) accept [`GooglePlayAppOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#googleplayappoptions) (`-g, --google-key`, `--package-name`), falling back to `GOOGLE_KEY`, `GOOGLE_PACKAGE_NAME` in `.env`, or auto-detection from the local Android project.

The default local folder is `~/.appitool/assets/<package-name>/google/`. When [`STORE_ASSETS_PATH`](https://appitool.appibara.com/guide/configuration#store-assets-apple-assets-google-assets) is set, it is `<STORE_ASSETS_PATH>/google/` instead (default paths below then refer to that folder).

> [!NOTE]
> **CI Guard:** Destructive subcommands (`assets delete`, `users delete`, `invitations cancel`, `users revoke`) accept [`GlobalCIOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#globalcioptions) (`--ci` / `--no-ci`) and are skipped as a no-op (exit code `0`) when running in CI mode. Pass `--no-ci` to force execution in CI.

## Synopsis

```bash
appitool google <resource> <action> [options]
```

## Subcommands Summary

| Domain | Subcommand | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Apps** | `apps list` | Lists apps accessible with the service account key (package name and Play Console title). |
| | `signing-certs list` | Shows SHA-1 / SHA-256 of Play App Signing certificates (incl. hybrid post-quantum) from Play-generated APKs or local certificate files. |
| **Store Visuals (`assets`)** | `assets list` | Lists existing store screenshots and graphic assets by locale and image type. |
| | `assets upload` | Uploads PNG/JPEG screenshots, icons, feature graphics, or banners and commits an edit. |
| | `assets download` | Downloads store screenshots and graphics locally to `~/.appitool/assets/<package>/google/` (or `-o`). |
| | `assets delete` | Deletes an individual image by ID or all images of a given type for a locale. |
| | `assets types` | Lists all supported Google Play `imageType` keys, aliases, and descriptions. |
| **Store Listing Text (`metadata`)** | `metadata list` | Shows title, short/full description, and video per language. |
| | `metadata download` | Writes listing text to `<locale>/metadata/<field>.txt` files. |
| | `metadata upload` | Sends changed fields in one edit and commits it. |
| **Users** | `users list` | Lists developer account users with account and per-app permissions. |
| | `users invite` | Invites a user (account permissions and/or access to one app). |
| | `users update` | Changes a user's account permissions or access expiration. |
| | `users delete` | Removes a user. |
| | `users grant` | Gives a user permissions for one app (creates or replaces the grant). |
| | `users revoke` | Removes a user's permissions for one app. |
| **Invitations** | `invitations list` | Lists pending or expired invitations. |
| | `invitations cancel` | Cancels a pending invitation. |

---

## Supported Store Visual Types

| CLI Key | Aliases | API `imageType` | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `phone` | `phone-screenshots`, `phone_screenshots` | `phoneScreenshots` | Phone screenshots (PNG/JPEG, 2–8 images) |
| `tablet7` | `seven-inch`, `7-inch`, `seven-inch-screenshots` | `sevenInchScreenshots` | 7-inch tablet screenshots (PNG/JPEG) |
| `tablet10` | `ten-inch`, `10-inch`, `ten-inch-screenshots` | `tenInchScreenshots` | 10-inch tablet screenshots (PNG/JPEG) |
| `tv` | `tv-screenshots`, `tv_screenshots` | `tvScreenshots` | Android TV screenshots (PNG/JPEG) |
| `wear` | `watch`, `wear-screenshots`, `wear_screenshots` | `wearScreenshots` | Wear OS screenshots (PNG/JPEG) |
| `icon` | `app-icon` | `icon` | High-res app icon (512x512 PNG/JPEG) |
| `feature-graphic` | `feature`, `feature_graphic` | `featureGraphic` | Feature graphic banner (1024x500 PNG/JPEG) |
| `tv-banner` | `banner`, `tv_banner` | `tvBanner` | Android TV banner (1280x720 PNG/JPEG) |

## Screenshots & Visuals (`appitool google assets`)

### `appitool google assets list`

Opens a temporary read-only Google Play edit session (deleted automatically after reading), lists configured store listing languages (or the specified `--locale`), and prints images for each matching `(language, imageType)` slot.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--locale <bcp47>` | Filter by BCP-47 language code (e.g. `en-US`, `tr-TR`). Omit to inspect all listing languages. |
| `-t, --type <type>` | Filter by image type (e.g. `phone`, `tablet7`, `feature-graphic`, `icon`). Omit to inspect all types. |

```bash
appitool google assets list --package-name com.example.app
appitool google assets list --locale en-US -t phone
```

### `appitool google assets upload`

Uploads PNG/JPEG screenshots and graphics to Google Play Console inside a single atomic edit transaction—either for flat image path(s) (`--locale` required, `-t` defaults to `phone`) or symmetrically from a `<locale>/<type>/` directory tree defaulting to `~/.appitool/assets/<package-name>/google/` (`--locale` and `-t` optional filters).

| Option / Flag / Argument | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--locale <bcp47>` | — | BCP-47 language code (e.g. `en-US`, `tr-TR`). Required for flat files; optional filter for `<locale>/<type>/` trees. |
| `-t, --type <type>` | `phone` (flat) / all (tree) | Target image type (`phone`, `tablet7`, `tablet10`, `tv`, `wear`, `icon`, `feature-graphic`, `tv-banner`). |
| `--replace` | `false` | Delete existing images in each target slot before uploading. For `<locale>/<type>/` trees, also writes each folder's sync manifest after a committed edit. |
| `--sync` | `false` | Mirror `<locale>/<type>/` folders onto their slots using `.appitool-manifest.json` in a single edit (see [Image sync](#image-sync)). Cannot be combined with `--replace`; requires a directory tree, not explicit files or a flat folder. |
| `--validate-only` | `false` | Validate the edit session (`edits.validate`) without committing changes. |
| `--changes-not-sent-for-review` | `false` | Commit changes without automatically sending them for Google Play review. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate local image files and preview target slots without contacting Google Play. With `--sync`, reads Google Play in a discarded edit and prints the sync plan. |
| `<paths...>` | `~/.appitool/assets/<package-name>/google/` | Optional PNG/JPEG file(s), flat directory, or `<locale>/<type>/` directory tree. |

```bash
# Bulk-upload all locales and image types from ~/.appitool/assets/<package-name>/google/
appitool google assets upload --replace

# Bulk-upload only phone screenshots across all locales in the default folder
appitool google assets upload -t phone --replace

# Replace phone screenshots for en-US from a flat directory
appitool google assets upload \
  --package-name com.example.app \
  --locale en-US \
  -t phone \
  --replace \
  ./screenshots/android/en-US/phone/

# Upload a feature graphic banner
appitool google assets upload \
  --package-name com.example.app \
  --locale en-US \
  -t feature-graphic \
  ./assets/feature-graphic.png

# Preview, then apply, only the local changes since the last download/sync
appitool google assets upload --sync --dry-run
appitool google assets upload --sync
```

#### Image sync

`download`, `upload --replace` (directory trees), and `upload --sync` write a `.appitool-manifest.json` into each `<locale>/<type>/` folder. For every file it records the SHA-256 of the local file and Google Play's image `sha256`; remote images are matched by that hash.

Local files are classified the same way as for [`apple assets upload --sync`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/apple#asset-sync): unchanged (including renamed with the same content), edited, new, and removed. Because Google Play has no reorder call and appends uploads, each slot is rebuilt from the first position that differs:

1. Keep the longest leading run of images that are unchanged and already in place.
2. Delete every remote image after that run.
3. Upload the remaining local files in file-name order (unchanged files after the first change are re-uploaded from the local file).

Examples: editing the 6th of 8 phone screenshots deletes and uploads 6–8; appending a new last file uploads only that file; editing the 1st file re-uploads the whole slot.

All slots are planned first; any planning error aborts before an edit with changes is opened. All changes are applied in one edit and committed once, so a failure leaves Google Play unchanged. Manifests are rewritten only after a successful commit (not with `--validate-only`).

| Rule | Behavior |
|:---|:---|
| No manifest, remote slot empty | Bootstrap: upload all files in file-name order and write the manifest. |
| No manifest, remote slot has images | Error: run `download` first or use `--replace`. |
| Manifest for a different slot | Error: run `download` again or delete the manifest and use `--replace`. |
| Remote image not in the manifest after the first change | Error (it cannot be re-uploaded): run `download` again or use `--replace`. |
| Limits | Phone 2–8, other screenshot types up to 8, `icon` / `feature-graphic` / `tv-banner` exactly 1. |

A `<locale>/<type>/` folder with no images is skipped, so emptying a folder does not clear its slot; use `google assets delete` for that.

### `appitool google assets download`

Downloads store screenshots and graphics from Google Play Console into `<output>/<locale>/<type>/01.<ext>` (rewriting CDN URLs to `=s0` for full original resolution). Opens a short-lived read-only edit session that is deleted before downloading binaries. By default, files are stored per project under `~/.appitool/assets/<package-name>/google/`.

Each slot folder also gets a `.appitool-manifest.json` for [`upload --sync`](#image-sync). Images written by a previous download that are no longer on Google Play are removed; other local images are kept and reported (`upload --sync` would add them).

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--locale <bcp47>` | — | Filter by BCP-47 language code (e.g. `en-US`, `tr-TR`). Omit to download all listing languages. |
| `-t, --type <type>` | — | Filter by image type (e.g. `phone`, `tablet7`, `feature-graphic`, `icon`). Omit to download all types. |
| `-o, --output <dir>` | `~/.appitool/assets/<package-name>/google/` | Custom destination root directory. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Preview target local paths and CDN URLs without downloading files. |

```bash
# Download all Google Play visuals to ~/.appitool/assets/<package-name>/google/
appitool google assets download

# Download only en-US phone screenshots into a custom folder
appitool google assets download --package-name com.example.app --locale en-US -t phone -o ./downloads/android
```

### `appitool google assets delete`

Deletes a specific image by ID or all images of a given type for a locale in Google Play Console (guarded in CI mode).

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--locale <bcp47>` | **Required** | BCP-47 language code (e.g. `en-US`, `tr-TR`). |
| `-t, --type <type>` | **Required** | Target image type (`phone`, `tablet7`, `tablet10`, `tv`, `wear`, `icon`, `feature-graphic`, `tv-banner`). |
| `--id <image-id>` | — | Specific Google Play image ID to delete (mutually exclusive with `--all`). |
| `--all` | `false` | Delete all images of the specified type for the language (mutually exclusive with `--id`). |
| `--changes-not-sent-for-review` | `false` | Commit changes without automatically sending them for Google Play review. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Preview matching image(s) without deleting or committing changes. |

```bash
# Preview images that would be removed
appitool google assets delete --locale en-US -t phone --all --dry-run

# Delete a single image by ID
appitool google assets delete --locale en-US -t phone --id AO7oq_example_id
```

### `appitool google assets types`

Prints all supported Google Play `imageType` keys, aliases, API names, and descriptions (no credentials required).

```bash
appitool google assets types
```

---

## Metadata (`appitool google metadata`)

Manages Google Play store listing text as one plain-text file per field: `<root>/<locale>/metadata/<field>.txt`, where `<root>` is `$STORE_ASSETS_PATH/google/` or `~/.appitool/assets/<package-name>/google/` (the same folder as `google assets`; image commands ignore `metadata/` folders). Store listings have no versions, so there is one current set of files per language. Release notes ("What's new") belong to track releases on Google Play and are not part of listing metadata.

| File | Field | Limit |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `title.txt` | Title | 30 |
| `short_description.txt` | Short description | 80 |
| `full_description.txt` | Full description | 4000 |
| `video.txt` | Promo video URL | — |

**App-level details** (one value for the app, `edits.details`) live in `<root>/metadata/<field>.txt`: `contact_email.txt`, `contact_phone.txt`, `contact_website.txt`, and `default_language.txt` (BCP-47, e.g. `en-US`).

### `appitool google metadata list`

Shows the app-level details (`[app]`) and every listing field per language with its character count and limit (read-only edit, discarded).

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--locale <bcp47>` | Show only this language (app-level details are skipped). |

### `appitool google metadata download`

Writes each non-empty field to `<locale>/metadata/<field>.txt` and the app-level details to `metadata/<field>.txt`. Existing files are overwritten.

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--locale <bcp47>` | — | Download only this language (app-level details are skipped). |
| `-o, --output <dir>` | `$STORE_ASSETS_PATH/google/` or `~/.appitool/assets/<package-name>/google/` | Metadata root directory. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Preview files without writing them. |

### `appitool google metadata upload`

Compares local files with the current listings and app details (surrounding whitespace ignored) and patches only fields that differ, all languages and the app details in one edit committed once. Missing and empty files are ignored. Length limits are checked before the edit is opened; nothing is sent when there are no changes. Local languages without a Play listing are skipped with a warning.

| Option / Flag / Argument | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--locale <bcp47>` | — | Upload only this language (app-level details are skipped). |
| `--validate-only` | `false` | Validate the edit (`edits.validate`) without committing. |
| `--changes-not-sent-for-review` | `false` | Commit without automatically sending the changes for review. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Print the per-field changes without opening an edit with changes. |
| `<path>` | `$STORE_ASSETS_PATH/google/` or `~/.appitool/assets/<package-name>/google/` | Metadata root containing `<locale>/metadata/` folders. |

```bash
appitool google metadata download
appitool google metadata upload --dry-run
appitool google metadata upload
```

---

## Apps

### `appitool google apps list`

Lists every app the service account can access, using the Play Developer Reporting API `apps.search` (`GET https://playdeveloperreporting.googleapis.com/v1beta1/apps:search`, all pages). Useful for finding package names (`GOOGLE_PACKAGE_NAME`) and checking that a key works. It does not return Play Console account IDs; no Google Play API exposes those (see [`GOOGLE_PLAY_ACCOUNT_ID`](https://appitool.appibara.com/guide/configuration)).

Requires the **Google Play Developer Reporting API** to be enabled in the service account's Google Cloud project (HTTP 403 otherwise) and access to the apps in Play Console. The title is the one set in Play Console and may not be live yet.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `-g, --google-key <key>` | Service account key (`GOOGLE_KEY`). |
| `-n, --name <text>` | Filter by app title (case-insensitive substring). |
| `-l, --limit <count>` | Maximum number of apps to show. |

```bash
appitool google apps list
appitool google apps list -n kokono
```

### `appitool google signing-certs list`

Shows the SHA-1 and SHA-256 fingerprints of the certificates Play App Signing uses, e.g. for Firebase, Google Sign-In, or `assetlinks.json`. Play Console's certificate download can contain three certificates: `deployment_cert.der` (app signing, RSA), `hybrid_classical_cert.der` (RSA), and `hybrid_pqc_cert.der` (post-quantum ML-DSA); all are covered.

**From the API (default):**

1. Reads the Play-generated APKs of a version code (`GET applications/{package}/generatedApks/{versionCode}`), grouped by signing key; the API reports each key's certificate SHA-256.
2. Downloads the smallest Play-generated APK per signing key (a config split of a few KB when available, otherwise a standalone or universal APK; held in memory only) and reads every certificate from its APK Signing Block — v2, v3, v3.1, the `hybrid` block (`0x70E1C89F`, Play's classical + post-quantum certificates; not in Android's public docs, identified from Play-generated APKs), and other unknown blocks (shown as `block 0x…`) — then prints SHA-1, SHA-256, and the algorithm (RSA, ECDSA, ML-DSA-44/65/87) of each and whether it matches the API's SHA-256.

Generated APKs exist for app bundles (AAB) uploaded with Play App Signing, so the API mode needs at least one uploaded AAB: with no release on any track the command exits with an explanation (pass `--version-code` for a bundle uploaded but not yet in a release). The service account needs release access to the app (HTTP 403 otherwise). The upload key certificate is not available through the API; it is your own keystore's certificate (`appitool match android`).

**From local files (`-f`):** fingerprints certificate files directly (DER `.der`/`.cer`/`.crt` or PEM `.pem`; folders are expanded), without any API call — for example the folder Play Console's certificate download creates. A fingerprint is the hash of the DER bytes, so this also works for post-quantum certificates that older tools such as `openssl` cannot parse.

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--package-name <name>` | `GOOGLE_PACKAGE_NAME` / project | App to inspect (API mode). |
| `--version-code <code>` | Highest version code on your tracks | Version code whose generated APKs are read. |
| `--sha256-only` | `false` | Only print the API's SHA-256 values (no APK download, no SHA-1). |
| `-f, --file <path>` | — | Certificate file or folder to fingerprint locally (repeatable). Skips the API. |
| `-g, --google-key <key>` | `GOOGLE_KEY` | Service account key (API mode). |

```bash
# Fingerprints from Play (latest version code)
appitool google signing-certs list

# Fingerprints of the certificates downloaded from Play Console
appitool google signing-certs list -f ~/Downloads/certificates
```

---

## Users & Invitations

Manages Play Console users of the developer account through the Play Developer API `users` and `grants` resources. A user has account-wide permissions (`developerAccountPermissions`) and per-app grants (`appLevelPermissions`). Google has no separate invitation object: an invited user has `accessState` `INVITED` (or `INVITATION_EXPIRED`) until they accept.

All user commands accept `-g, --google-key` (`GOOGLE_KEY`) and `--account-id <id>` (`GOOGLE_PLAY_ACCOUNT_ID`): your Play Console account ID, the number in `play.google.com/console/developers/<id>` (not the Google Cloud project, service account, or package name). The service account needs the **Manage users and permissions** (admin) permission in Play Console; API errors are shown with a likely cause (e.g. 403 → missing permission or wrong account ID).

**Permission values** are comma-separated and case-insensitive, written as `can-see-all-apps` or `CAN_SEE_ALL_APPS`:

- Account-wide (`--permissions` on `users invite` / `users update`; the `_GLOBAL` suffix is optional): `can-see-all-apps`, `can-view-financial-data`, `can-manage-permissions`, `can-edit-games`, `can-publish-games`, `can-reply-to-reviews`, `can-manage-public-apks`, `can-manage-track-apks`, `can-manage-track-users`, `can-manage-public-listing`, `can-manage-draft-apps`, `can-create-managed-play-apps`, `can-change-managed-play-setting`, `can-manage-orders`, `can-manage-app-content`, `can-view-non-financial-data`, `can-view-app-quality`, `can-manage-deeplinks`, `can-view-connected-apps`, `can-edit-connected-apps`.
- Per app (`--app-permissions` on `users invite`, `--permissions` on `users grant`): `can-access-app`, `can-view-financial-data`, `can-manage-permissions`, `can-reply-to-reviews`, `can-manage-public-apks`, `can-manage-track-apks`, `can-manage-track-users`, `can-manage-public-listing`, `can-manage-draft-apps`, `can-manage-orders`, `can-manage-app-content`, `can-view-non-financial-data`, `can-view-app-quality`, `can-manage-deeplinks`.

Some of these values are returned by the live API but missing from Google's API spec; they are accepted as well.

| Command | Options | Notes |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `users list` | `-e, --email`, `-l, --limit` | Users who accepted (state `ACCESS_GRANTED` / `ACCESS_EXPIRED`), with account permissions, expiration, and per-app grants. |
| `invitations list` | `-e, --email`, `-l, --limit` | Users in `INVITED` / `INVITATION_EXPIRED` state. |
| `users invite` | `-e, --email` (required), `--permissions`, `--package-name` + `--app-permissions`, `--expiration <iso8601>` | At least one of `--permissions` or `--app-permissions` is required; `--package-name` and `--app-permissions` go together. The app grant is created right after the invitation. |
| `users update` | `-e, --email` (required), `--permissions`, `--expiration <iso8601>` | Replaces the account-wide permissions and/or sets a new (future) expiration. Per-app permissions use `users grant` / `users revoke`. |
| `users delete` | `-e, --email` (required) | Removes the user. Destructive (CI-guarded). |
| `invitations cancel` | `-e, --email` (required) | Only for users who have not accepted yet; otherwise use `users delete`. Destructive (CI-guarded). |
| `users grant` | `-e, --email` (required), `--package-name` (`GOOGLE_PACKAGE_NAME` / project), `--permissions` (required) | Creates the app grant, or replaces its permissions if the user already has one. The user must exist (invite first). |
| `users revoke` | `-e, --email` (required), `--package-name` | Removes the user's grant for that app. Destructive (CI-guarded). |

```bash
appitool google users list
appitool google users invite -e dev@example.com --package-name com.example.app --app-permissions can-access-app,can-manage-track-apks
appitool google users grant -e dev@example.com --permissions can-access-app,can-reply-to-reviews
appitool google users update -e dev@example.com --expiration 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z
appitool google invitations cancel -e dev@example.com
```

---

<!-- source: commands/firebase.md -->

# `appitool firebase`

Manages Firebase apps (iOS, Android, web), App Distribution releases and tester groups, Firebase Authentication user accounts, and Cloud Firestore collections and documents.

> [!NOTE]
> **CI Guard:** Destructive subcommands (`apps delete`, `users delete`, and `firestore delete`) accept [`GlobalCIOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#globalcioptions) (`--ci` / `--no-ci`) and are skipped as a no-op (exit code `0`) when running in CI mode. Pass `--no-ci` to force execution in CI.

## Synopsis

```bash
appitool firebase <resource> <action> [options]
```

## Subcommands Summary

| Domain | Subcommand | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Apps** | `apps list` | Lists the iOS, Android, and web apps registered in a Firebase project. |
| | `apps create` | Registers an iOS, Android, or web app (reports the existing app if already registered). |
| | `apps delete` | Removes an app (restorable for 30 days unless `--immediate`). |
| | `fingerprints sync` | Adds the Play App Signing SHA-1/SHA-256 fingerprints to a Firebase Android app. |
| **App Distribution** | `releases list` | Lists uploaded releases for a Firebase App ID. |
| | `releases create` | Uploads an `.apk`, `.aab`, or `.ipa` binary, attaches notes, and distributes to groups/testers. |
| | `releases update` | Updates release notes or distributes an existing release to tester groups/emails. |
| | `groups list` | Lists tester groups registered in a Firebase project. |
| | `groups create` | Creates a new tester group or retrieves an existing one by alias. |
| **Authentication** | `users list` | Lists Firebase Auth users with search, anonymous filter, and pagination. |
| | `users delete` | Deletes user(s) by UID, email, or bulk-deletes all anonymous users. |
| | `users export` | Exports Firebase Auth users to a CSV file. |
| **Cloud Firestore** | `firestore collections` | Lists root collection IDs or subcollections under a document path. |
| | `firestore list` | Lists documents in a Firestore collection. |
| | `firestore get` | Fetches a single Firestore document by path. |
| | `firestore set` | Creates or updates a Firestore document (supports `--merge` and auto-ID creation). |
| | `firestore delete` | Deletes a Firestore document by path (supports `--dry-run`). |
| | `firestore query` | Runs structured queries with `--where`, `--order-by`, `--limit`, and `--all-descendants`. |

---

## Firebase Apps Commands

Uses the Firebase Management API (`projects.searchApps`, `projects.{iosApps|androidApps|webApps}.create` / `.remove`, and `projects.androidApps.sha`). The service account needs a role that can manage Firebase apps in the project (e.g. Firebase Admin).

### `appitool firebase apps list`

Uses [`FirebaseProjectOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#firebaseprojectoptions) (`-g, --google-key`, `--project`).

Lists every app of the project grouped by platform, with display name, bundle ID / package name, and Firebase App ID (all pages).

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-p, --platform <platform>` | all | Only list `ios`, `android`, or `web` apps. |
| `--show-deleted` | `false` | Also list apps deleted within the last 30 days. |

```bash
appitool firebase apps list -p ios
```

### `appitool firebase apps create`

Uses [`FirebaseProjectOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#firebaseprojectoptions).

Registers an app in the project and waits for Firebase to finish creating it, then prints its Firebase App ID and the `.env` variable to set (`FIREBASE_IOS_APP_ID` / `FIREBASE_ANDROID_APP_ID`). If an app with the same platform and bundle ID / package name is already registered, it is reported instead of created.

| Option | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-p, --platform <platform>` | **Required** | `ios`, `android`, or `web`. |
| `-b, --bundle-id <id>` | `APPLE_BUNDLE_ID` / Xcode project | iOS bundle identifier (`-p ios` only). |
| `--package-name <name>` | `GOOGLE_PACKAGE_NAME` / Android project | Android package name (`-p android` only). |
| `-n, --name <display>` | — | Display name in Firebase (required for `-p web`). |
| `--app-store-id <id>` | — | Apple ID of the app in the App Store (`-p ios` only). |
| `--team-id <id>` | — | Apple Developer Team ID (`-p ios` only). |
| `--sha1 <hex>` | — | SHA-1 certificate fingerprint to register, colons optional (`-p android` only; repeatable). |
| `--sha256 <hex>` | — | SHA-256 certificate fingerprint to register, colons optional (`-p android` only; repeatable). |

```bash
appitool firebase apps create -p ios -n "My App"
appitool firebase apps create -p android --package-name com.example.app --sha1 16:00:71:...
appitool firebase apps create -p web -n "My Web App"
```

### `appitool firebase apps delete`

Uses [`FirebaseProjectOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#firebaseprojectoptions) and [`GlobalCIOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#globalcioptions) (skipped in CI unless `--no-ci`).

Removes an app from the project. By default the removal can be undone in the Firebase console for 30 days; `--immediate` deletes it permanently. The app is chosen explicitly (the `FIREBASE_*_APP_ID` variables are not used as defaults).

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--firebase-app-id <id>` | — | Firebase App ID of the app to remove. |
| `-p, --platform <platform>` | — | `ios`, `android`, or `web`; used instead of `--firebase-app-id` with one of the next three options. |
| `-b, --bundle-id <id>` | — | iOS bundle identifier (`-p ios`). |
| `--package-name <name>` | — | Android package name (`-p android`). |
| `-n, --name <display>` | — | Display name of the web app (`-p web`). |
| `--immediate` | `false` | Delete permanently right away instead of the 30-day restorable removal. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate the removal with Firebase without removing the app. |

```bash
appitool firebase apps delete -p android --package-name com.example.app --dry-run
appitool firebase apps delete --firebase-app-id 1:123456789:ios:abc123
```

### `appitool firebase fingerprints sync`

Uses [`FirebaseProjectOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#firebaseprojectoptions). The same service account key (`-g, --google-key` / `GOOGLE_KEY`) is used for Google Play and Firebase, so it needs release access to the app in Play Console and a Firebase role that can manage apps.

Registers certificate fingerprints on a Firebase Android app (needed for Google Sign-In, Phone Auth, Dynamic/App Links, etc.):

1. Reads the Play App Signing certificates exactly like [`google signing-certs list`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/google#appitool-google-signing-certs-list) — the deployment certificate and the hybrid classical + post-quantum certificates — and takes the SHA-1 and SHA-256 of each. If an APK cannot be read, only the API's SHA-256 is used for that key.
2. Adds certificates from `-f, --file` (e.g. your upload or debug certificate) and fingerprints from `--sha1` / `--sha256`.
3. Compares with the app's registered fingerprints and adds the missing ones. Existing fingerprints are kept unless `--replace` is passed.

The Firebase app is `--firebase-app-id`, else `FIREBASE_ANDROID_APP_ID`, else the Android app registered for the package name. Download a fresh `google-services.json` afterwards if your build embeds it.

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--firebase-app-id <id>` | `FIREBASE_ANDROID_APP_ID` / app for the package name | Firebase Android App ID. |
| `--package-name <name>` | `GOOGLE_PACKAGE_NAME` / Android project | Android package name (Play lookup and app lookup). |
| `--version-code <code>` | Highest version code on your tracks | Version code whose Play-generated APKs are read. |
| `--play` / `--no-play` | `--play` | Read the Play App Signing certificates from Google Play. `--no-play` needs `-f`, `--sha1`, or `--sha256`. |
| `-f, --file <path>` | — | Additional certificate file or folder to register (`.der`/`.cer`/`.crt`/`.pem`; repeatable). |
| `--sha1 <hex>` | — | Additional SHA-1 fingerprint (repeatable; colons optional). |
| `--sha256 <hex>` | — | Additional SHA-256 fingerprint (repeatable; colons optional). |
| `--replace` | `false` | Also remove registered fingerprints that are not in the synced set. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Show the changes without applying them. |

```bash
# Add the Play App Signing fingerprints (deployment + hybrid)
appitool firebase fingerprints sync

# Also register the upload certificate, preview first
appitool firebase fingerprints sync -f upload_cert.der --dry-run
```

## App Distribution Commands

All three release subcommands use [`FirebaseCredentialsOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#firebasecredentialsoptions) (`--firebase-app-id`, `-p, --platform`, `-g, --google-key`, `--project`).

### `appitool firebase releases list`

Lists uploaded releases for a Firebase application (version, build, creation timestamp, release notes, and console URI).

| Option | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-l, --limit <count>` | `25` | Maximum number of releases to return (`1–100`). |
| `--order-by <expr>` | — | Ordering expression (e.g. `'createTime desc'`). |

```bash
appitool firebase releases list --platform ios -l 10
```

### `appitool firebase releases create`

Uploads an `.apk`, `.aab`, or `.ipa` binary to Firebase App Distribution, waits for processing, optionally attaches release notes, and distributes to tester groups/emails.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--binary <path>` | Path to `.apk`, `.aab`, or `.ipa` binary (**Required**). |
| `--release-notes <text>` | Release notes text for testers. |
| `--test-groups <aliases>` | Comma-separated tester group aliases (e.g. `'internal,qa'`). Missing groups are created automatically before upload. |
| `--tester-emails <emails>` | Comma-separated tester email addresses. |

```bash
appitool firebase releases create \
  --platform android \
  --binary ./app-release.apk \
  --release-notes "QA build #42" \
  --test-groups "internal,qa"
```

### `appitool firebase releases update`

Updates an existing Firebase App Distribution release by attaching new release notes and/or distributing to tester groups or emails.

| Option | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `--release-id <id>` | Full release resource path (`projects/.../apps/.../releases/<id>`) or short release ID (**Required**; `--firebase-app-id` is required if passing a short ID). |
| `--release-notes <text>` | New release notes text to attach. |
| `--test-groups <aliases>` | Comma-separated tester group aliases to distribute to. |
| `--tester-emails <emails>` | Comma-separated tester emails to distribute to. |

```bash
appitool firebase releases update \
  --platform ios \
  --release-id 1a2b3c4d5e \
  --release-notes "Updated notes" \
  --test-groups "internal"
```

### `appitool firebase groups list`

Uses [`FirebaseProjectOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#firebaseprojectoptions) (`-g, --google-key`, `--project`).

Lists tester groups registered in a Firebase project with alias, tester count, and release count.

| Option | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-l, --limit <count>` | `25` | Maximum number of groups to return (`1–1000`). |

### `appitool firebase groups create`

Uses [`FirebaseProjectOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#firebaseprojectoptions).

Creates a new tester group (or returns the existing group if the alias already exists).

| Option | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--alias <alias>` | **Required** | Unique alias/ID for the group (e.g. `internal`, `qa-team`). |
| `-n, --name <display>` | `<alias>` | Human-readable display name (e.g. `'Internal Testers'`). |

```bash
appitool firebase groups create --alias qa-team -n "QA Team"
```

## Firebase Authentication Commands

All user management subcommands use [`FirebaseProjectOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#firebaseprojectoptions) (`-g, --google-key`, `--project`).

### `appitool firebase users list`

Lists Firebase Authentication users with optional exact/partial search by email or UID, anonymous filtering, and pagination token support.

| Option | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-l, --limit <count>` | `100` | Maximum number of users to return. |
| `--search <query>` | — | Search users by email or UID (attempts fast exact lookup on page 1 before paginated scan). |
| `--anonymous <filter>` | `all` | Filter by anonymous status: `all`, `only`, or `exclude`. |
| `--page-token <token>` | — | Pagination token printed at the end of the previous page output. |

```bash
# List up to 50 non-anonymous users
appitool firebase users list -l 50 --anonymous exclude

# Search for a user by email
appitool firebase users list --search user@example.com
```

### `appitool firebase users delete`

Deletes Firebase Authentication user(s) by UID, by email lookup, or deletes all anonymous accounts in batches of 500.

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--uid <uid>` | — | UID (`localId`) of the user to delete. |
| `-e, --email <email>` | — | Email address of the user to look up and delete. |
| `--anonymous` | `false` | Delete all anonymous users in the project (cannot be combined with `--uid` or `-e`). |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Preview matching user(s) without deleting them. |

```bash
# Preview bulk anonymous user cleanup
appitool firebase users delete --anonymous --dry-run

# Delete a specific user by email
appitool firebase users delete -e tester@example.com
```

### `appitool firebase users export`

Exports all Firebase Authentication users to a UTF-8 CSV file with columns:
`uid,email,email_verified,display_name,phone_number,photo_url,is_anonymous,disabled,providers,created_at,last_login_at`.

| Option | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--anonymous <filter>` | `all` | Filter exported users: `all`, `only`, or `exclude`. |
| `-o, --output <path>` | `firebase_users_<project>.csv` | Output CSV filename or path. |

```bash
appitool firebase users export --anonymous exclude -o ./exports/users.csv
```

## Cloud Firestore Commands

All `appitool firebase firestore` subcommands use [`FirebaseProjectOptions`](https://appitool.appibara.com/commands/overview#firebaseprojectoptions) (`-g, --google-key`, `--project`) and `--database <id>` (defaults to `(default)`).

> [!NOTE]
> - **Project ID Resolution:** Firestore requires a string Google Cloud `project_id` resolved in order: `--project` → `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` / `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` → `project_id` embedded inside the `GOOGLE_KEY` Service Account JSON.
> - **IAM Permissions:** The Service Account must hold `Cloud Datastore Viewer` (`roles/datastore.viewer`) for read-only commands (`collections`, `list`, `get`, `query`) or `Cloud Datastore User` (`roles/datastore.user`) for read/write/delete commands (`set`, `delete`). Service Account requests bypass client Firestore Security Rules.

### `appitool firebase firestore collections`

Lists root collection IDs or subcollection IDs beneath a specific document path.

| Option / Argument | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `<path>` | — | Optional parent document path (even number of segments, e.g. `users/alice`). |
| `-l, --limit <count>` | `100` | Maximum number of collection IDs to return. |
| `--page-token <token>` | — | Pagination token to fetch the next page of collection IDs. |
| `--json` | `false` | Output raw JSON. |

```bash
appitool firebase firestore collections
appitool firebase firestore collections users/alice --json
```

### `appitool firebase firestore list`

Lists documents in a Firestore collection.

| Option / Argument | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `<path>` | **Required** | Firestore collection path (odd number of segments, e.g. `users` or `users/alice/orders`). |
| `-l, --limit <count>` | `50` | Maximum number of documents to return. |
| `--order-by <expr>` | — | Sort expression (e.g. `'createdAt desc'`). |
| `--page-token <token>` | — | Pagination token to fetch the next page of documents. |
| `--json` | `false` | Output raw JSON. |

```bash
appitool firebase firestore list users -l 20
```

### `appitool firebase firestore get`

Fetches a single Firestore document by path.

| Option / Argument | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `<path>` | **Required** | Firestore document path (even number of segments, e.g. `users/alice`). |
| `--json` | `false` | Output raw JSON. |

```bash
appitool firebase firestore get users/alice --json
```

### `appitool firebase firestore set`

Writes a document at a document path (`PATCH`, creating or overwriting) or creates a document with an auto-generated ID when given a collection path (`POST`).

| Option / Flag / Argument | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `<path>` | **Required** | Document path (`users/alice`) or collection path (`users`). |
| `--data <json>` | — | Inline JSON object string containing document fields (mutually exclusive with `-f`). |
| `-f, --file <path>` | — | Path to a JSON file containing document fields (mutually exclusive with `--data`). |
| `--merge` | `false` | Merge provided top-level fields using `updateMask.fieldPaths` (requires a document path). |
| `--json` | `false` | Output raw JSON. |

```bash
appitool firebase firestore set users/alice --data '{"role":"admin","active":true}' --merge
appitool firebase firestore set logs -f ./event.json
```

### `appitool firebase firestore delete`

Deletes a Firestore document by path.

| Option / Flag / Argument | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `<path>` | **Required** | Firestore document path (even number of segments, e.g. `users/alice`). |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Check whether the document exists without deleting it. |

```bash
appitool firebase firestore delete users/alice --dry-run
appitool firebase firestore delete users/alice
```

### `appitool firebase firestore query`

Runs a structured query (`:runQuery`) against a collection (or collection group when `--all-descendants` is set).

| Option / Flag / Argument | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `<path>` | **Required** | Firestore collection path (odd number of segments, e.g. `users` or `orders`). |
| `-w, --where <expr>` | — | Repeatable filter expression: `<field> <op> <value>`. Supported `<op>`: `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `array-contains`, `in`, `not-in`, `array-contains-any`. |
| `--order-by <expr>` | — | Repeatable sort clause (`<field> [asc\|desc]`). |
| `-l, --limit <count>` | `50` | Maximum number of documents to return. |
| `--all-descendants` | `false` | Query across all descendant collections matching the final collection ID (collection group query). |
| `--json` | `false` | Output raw JSON. |

```bash
appitool firebase firestore query users \
  -w 'active == true' \
  -w 'age >= 18' \
  --order-by 'age desc' \
  -l 10 \
  --json
```

<!-- source: commands/inspect.md -->

# `appitool inspect`

Inspects local iOS (Xcode) and Android (Gradle) project files in a workspace and prints resolved identifiers, versions, build numbers / version codes, targets, schemes, and product flavors. When `-s, --scheme` is omitted on iOS, all distributable schemes are inspected and listed; when `--flavor` is omitted on Android, all product flavors are listed with their effective application IDs, versions, and version codes.

## Synopsis

```bash
appitool inspect [options]
```

## Options & Flags

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-p, --platform <platform>` | `all` | Platform to inspect: `all`, `ios`, or `android`. |
| `--workspace-name <name>` | Auto-detected | Custom Xcode workspace or project name. |
| `-s, --scheme <scheme>` | All distributable schemes | Specific Xcode scheme name to inspect (omit to list every distributable scheme). |
| `-c, --configuration <config>` | Auto-inferred | Xcode build configuration (e.g., `Debug`, `Release`). |
| `--flavor <name>` | All product flavors | Specific Android product flavor to resolve (omit to list all `productFlavors` with resolved overrides). |
| `--project-dir <path>` | Current directory | Path to the project root directory. |
| `--json` | `false` | Output results as pretty-printed, key-sorted JSON (`ios.schemes[]`, `ios.version`, `ios.buildNumber`, `android.versionName`, `android.versionCode`, and resolved `android.flavors[]`). |

## Examples

```bash
# Inspect all iOS schemes and all Android flavors (including versions and build numbers)
appitool inspect

# Inspect a single iOS scheme as JSON
appitool inspect -p ios -s MyApp -c Release --json

# Inspect Android metadata filtered to a single product flavor
appitool inspect -p android --flavor staging

# Inspect a project located in another directory
appitool inspect --project-dir ~/projects/my-mobile-app
```

<!-- source: commands/clean.md -->

# `appitool clean`

Scans `~/.appitool/ios` and `~/.appitool/android` and deletes previously built archives (`.xcarchive`, `.ipa`, `.aab`, `.apk`), optional Xcode DerivedData directories, and (with `--assets`) downloaded store assets under `~/.appitool/assets` (plus the legacy `~/.appitool/screenshots` folder used by older versions). System folders such as `~/.appitool/android/keystores` and `tmp` are preserved, and asset folders are only touched with `--assets`.

## Synopsis

```bash
appitool clean [options]
```

## Options & Flags

| Option / Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `-p, --platform <platform>` | `all` | Platform to clean: `ios`, `android`, or `all`. |
| `--dd, --derived-data` | `false` | Also clean Xcode `derivedData` directories under `~/.appitool/ios/<project>/derivedData`. |
| `--ddo, --derived-data-only` | `false` | Only clean Xcode `derivedData` directories without deleting build archives. |
| `--assets` | `false` | Also clean downloaded store assets (screenshots, header/search images, Google Play graphics, their sync manifests, and downloaded `metadata/` text files) under `~/.appitool/assets/<project>/<store>/` and the legacy `~/.appitool/screenshots/<project>/<store>/` (removed once empty). A custom `STORE_ASSETS_PATH` folder is never cleaned (it usually lives in your project). `-p ios` limits it to `apple`, `-p android` to `google`, `all` cleans every store folder. Combined with `--ddo`, cleans derived data and assets but no build archives. |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Scan and display items with disk sizes without deleting anything. |

## Examples

```bash
# Preview all build artifacts and Xcode DerivedData that would be removed
appitool clean --derived-data --dry-run

# Delete all iOS and Android build artifacts (keeps DerivedData)
appitool clean

# Delete only Xcode DerivedData directories
appitool clean --ddo

# Clean only Android build outputs
appitool clean -p android

# Preview build artifacts plus downloaded App Store assets for iOS
appitool clean -p ios --assets --dry-run
```

<!-- source: commands/notes.md -->

# `appitool notes`

Generates categorized Markdown release notes from Git commit history between two tags or revisions (`git log --no-merges`).

## How Commits Are Categorized

`GenerateReleaseNotesTask` parses Conventional Commit prefixes (`type(scope): description`):
- `feat` → **`### 🚀 Features`**
- `fix` → **`### 🐛 Bug Fixes`**
- All other commit types / non-conventional commits → **`### 🔧 Other Changes`**

Within each category, scoped commits are grouped under `* **<scope>**:`, and commit hashes are automatically formatted as clickable Markdown links when `remote.origin.url` resolves to an HTTP/HTTPS/SSH Git host (e.g. `([#abc1234](https://github.com/org/repo/commit/abc1234))`).

## Synopsis

```bash
appitool notes [options]
```

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--from <ref>` | Latest Git tag at or before `--to` (or last 20 commits if untagged) | Starting Git tag or commit reference (exclusive). If omitted and `--to` (or `HEAD`) already sits on a matching tag, no commits are returned; pass `--from` explicitly to inspect a tagged release. |
| `--to <ref>` | `HEAD` | Ending Git tag or commit reference (inclusive). |
| `--tag-prefix <prefix>` | — | Filter auto-detected tags by prefix when `--from` is omitted (e.g. `v`, `ios-v`, `android-`). |
| `-o, --output <path>` | Print to stdout | File path to write the generated Markdown release notes. |

## Examples

```bash
# Auto-detect commits since the latest Git tag (or last 20 commits if untagged)
appitool notes

# Auto-detect commits since the latest iOS-prefixed tag (e.g. ios-v1.2.0..HEAD)
appitool notes --tag-prefix ios-v

# Print release notes from v0.8.0 to HEAD
appitool notes --from v0.8.0

# Generate notes between two tags and save to CHANGELOG_DRAFT.md
appitool notes --from v0.8.0 --to v0.9.0 -o CHANGELOG_DRAFT.md
```

<!-- source: commands/kokono.md -->

# `appitool kokono`

Dispatches a push notification to a KokoNo webhook endpoint (`?token=<token>`), with optional end-to-end (E2E) encryption.

## End-to-End Encryption & Keypair Isolation

- When an E2E public key is resolved (Base64-encoded 32-byte Curve25519 / X25519 public key), `NotifyTask` encrypts both `title` and `message` using an ephemeral X25519 key pair + `HKDF-SHA256` (`salt: "kokono-salt-v1"`, `info: "kokono-info-v1"`) + `AES-256-GCM`.
- Messages longer than 250 characters are truncated with `...`.
- **Per-URL Keypair Isolation**: If `--url` is explicitly passed on the command line, `appitool kokono` will **not** fall back to `KOKONO_E2E_PUBLIC_KEY` from `.env`—you must also pass `--e2e` explicitly if you want encryption for that custom URL.

## Synopsis

```bash
appitool kokono -m <message> [options]
```

## Options

| Option | Default / `.env` Fallback | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--title <title>` | `appitool` | Notification title. |
| `-m, --message <message>` | **Required** | Notification message body. |
| `--url <url>` | `KOKONO_URL` | KokoNo notification webhook URL (`https://kokono.me/notify?token=...`). |
| `--e2e <public-key>` | `KOKONO_E2E_PUBLIC_KEY` (when `--url` is omitted) | Base64 X25519 public key for E2E encryption. |

## Examples

```bash
# Send plain notification using KOKONO_URL from .env
appitool kokono -m "Release v0.9.0 deployed to TestFlight."

# Send E2E encrypted notification with explicit title
appitool kokono --title "CI Alert" -m "Build #128 succeeded." --e2e "<base64_x25519_public_key>"
```

---

<!-- source: commands/self-update.md -->

# `appitool self-update`

Checks GitHub Releases (`appibara-ltd/appitool`) for a newer semantic version and upgrades the currently running `appitool` binary in place after verifying its SHA256 checksum against `checksums.txt`.

## How It Works

1. Queries `https://api.github.com/repos/appibara-ltd/appitool/releases/latest`.
2. Compares the remote tag (`SemanticVersion`) against the running binary's version.
3. Selects the matching archive for the current OS & CPU architecture:
   - `appitool-darwin-arm64.tar.gz` (or `universal`)
   - `appitool-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` / `appitool-linux-arm64.tar.gz`
4. Downloads the archive and `checksums.txt`, verifies the SHA256 digest, extracts `appitool`, and atomically swaps the executable (with rollback on failure).

> [!TIP]
> If you hit GitHub API rate limits (e.g., in CI or shared networks), export `GITHUB_TOKEN` (or `GH_TOKEN`) or configure `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `.env`.

## Synopsis

```bash
appitool self-update [options]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `--check` | `false` | Check whether an update is available without downloading or installing. |
| `--force` | `false` | Force download and re-installation even if already on the latest version. |

## Examples

```bash
# Check if a newer release exists
appitool self-update --check

# Upgrade to the latest release
appitool self-update

# Force reinstall (use sudo if installed into a root-owned /usr/local/bin)
sudo appitool self-update --force
```

<!-- source: commands/status.md -->

# `appitool status`

Displays the CLI tool name, purpose, and compiled version.

## Synopsis

```bash
appitool status
```

## Example Output

```text
Tool: appitool
Purpose: A unified CLI utility for Apple App Store Connect and Google Play operations.
Version: 0.11.0
```
